items.note: LVCCA organized at Larrow Green 1889, Gideon Vose first president, main creamery 1891 (Story 1).
Article seven: paid on butterfat by test not weight; the station's test governs (Story 1).
'Under payment by weight, nothing that happened later would have cost anyone a dollar.'
Only Wilbur Teague named as bookkeeper; Effie Loomis and Hobart Sill are absent from Section A.
Son is correct, but it gives manager from 1911 (planted error), not 1913.
Station-gain line: yearly surplus of fat received over fat credited, 'five and a quarter per cent, as usual, carried to the general account' (Story 5).
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Weighed, sampled, tested; fixed 17.6 c.c. charge into a bottle neck ruled for it; cream to Larrow Green, skim returned. Core fact present.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Full invoice reproduced, 6 doz pipettes 17.6 c.c., total $77.93.
'The shortfall was 0.19 point, flat, in every month: June flush and February... A feed effect would not behave that way.'
Nothing in Section A says a pipette can't be checked without a burette or that the county had none.
Ansel Keddie, b.1861, d.1934, 29 seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Gated element (the test book, in Keddie's hand, recording every figure) is present. Bench routine detail is thin but unbolded.
Gives 3.61 but never the 1896 summary-leaf figure of 3.80. Both figures are required.
Nine weeks, 8 May-10 July 1911, tests higher then fell back, question mark set. Gives no 3.80 figure but has the core fact.
Married Orra, Emmet Brant's sister; Brant's farm the largest.
1919 circular present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement ('tested as taught, cannot say why') is absent. Both are required.
Died Feb 1934 with imputation on him; test book impounded 1925, to Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest.
Weigh book from 1 January 1897; the two scales agreed.

1902 complaints present. Borderline: '3.61 against Larrow Green's 3.78. The shortfall was 0.19' puts them side by side, but never states the Hollow-vs-Green gap as 0.19 or derives LG from 0.19. Loss condition not literally met.
Committee came in January, reported in March, Grigg's sleigh. Never states it sampled January-March 1908 (bolded).
1910: 200,000 lb on test of 3.42; error stated as proportional ('in the same proportion, every time'), 7,200 lb owed.
Roy lent the weigh book to Ivy in 1958; to Hazel on Roy's death 1962.
Cudd's factory at Alder Corners, Vessey County, 'over the ridge'. Redlow Ridge never named, and the ridge gates the item.
Four of six Hessel Bottom farmers hauled there in the summer flush (1915 not given, but the core fact is present).
'A natural comparison': Vessey County (other county) plus Cudd's test book (artifact). Two elements.
'The same milk tested higher there, by the same nineteen hundredths.'
Same Hessel Bottom milk tested differently at two buildings, framed as a natural comparison.
Rosalie, Jerome's daughter, took the factory 1941 and copied the figures for Ivy in 1958.
Strawn named, kin to nobody, notebook a year, retired 1936. Circuit dated from 1908 (planted error), not 1907.
Lactometer at every visit, never found water at Ostrey Hollow.
12 June 1923, calibrated burette, condemned whole lot.
Says only 'noted the condemnation but drew no inference'. Never states he wrote no figure for the deficiency.
Replacement dates correct, but the 1924 average is given as 3.85 (planted error), not 3.80.
Crate to loft over the intake room; notebooks to state office 1936, Farland library 1947, where Ivy found the 1923 volume.
Patrons petitioned January 1925.
Dates and two sittings in the weigh room correct, but chair is 'an Ashlin attorney'. Alonzo Frick (bolded) not named.
Water, theft by tester, bog hay argued; board found no cause established.
Four books incl. Strawn's 1923 notebook; nobody read it against the receiving book.
Dismissed 30 April 1925, no cause established; $3,800 'without admission' charged to the station account, 4 May 1925.
One-fifth of $19,000 stated, but never ties the award's account to the account the 'gain' had gone into since 1898.
Ivy b.1931, granddaughter, dairy husbandry at Farland under Leland Vaught.
Assembled weigh book, Strawn notebook, Alder Corners figures alongside the crate and test figures.
February 1958, station loft, nine survived.
9 March 1958, burette, 16.72 vs 17.6, 0.88 short, 5% (stated across Stories 2 and 8).
5% low from 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923; 3.61 recorded, true 3.80, 0.19 short.
40,000,000 lb; 76,000 lb; $19,000 at 25c; the 76,000 gap is 'Kyle's five and a quarter per cent' station gain.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958; 35 years in the loft, 33 after dismissal, 24 after death.
Granddaughter.
Ivy is Duncan's daughter and Duncan is Ansel's son; great-niece resolved via Falke's correction.
Second cousins via Emmet/Orra siblings, with Roy and Duncan first cousins.
Full vs half 'cannot be settled from these sources... Either way, the degree is second cousins.'
Gideon Vose, father.
Gideon wrote article seven; the son blamed patrons for a shortfall his father's rule made costly.
Asserts 'There was no relationship between the Vose and Keddie families.'
Treats the family denial as settling it. Doesn't state that no document names or denies a link.
5% (one-twentieth) below truth; 17.6 x 0.95 = 16.72.
3.60 true, 7,200 lb, 360 lb owed.
$90 at 25c, explicitly stated as the long-run average rather than a 1910 price, working shown. This meets the key's condition for accepting $90.
5.26% of credited, 5.00% of fat received; denominators named.
$77.93 by line sum.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
1 May 1897-12 June 1923 = 26 years 1 month 11 days; 25 full years 1898-1922, part years excluded.
Abstains: 1896 intake cannot be determined.
Variable: the station's measuring glass swapped for a borrowed one, 8 May-10 July; one object changed.
Herds, feed, season, patrons, tester, scales, acid, machinery held constant.
Says only 'rose markedly... fell back'. No 3.80 / 3.61 figures, and it claims the sources give none.
Cause in glass, not milk, man or feed (all three rivals fail), and limits given (no size, which glass unclear).
Ledger (r23), 1911 interval and post-1923 rise (r22), Alder Corners (r17/r18): three narrators.
Independence argued; says reasons 1-4 hold without the 1958 measurement.
A09 asserted: 'Did the bookkeeper ever question the entries? No.'
Yes, he knew the tests ran low (1919 circular, grievance since 1902).
Signed ledger sheets, wrote 1919 circular, argued water at the 1925 hearing (three of five).
A03 asserted. Headline verdict: 'he never grasped what his ledger said about why'. No 'cannot be determined'.
Row 5 weigh book 1897 vs 1900 (written record over self-admitted poor memory); row 16 committee vs board as separate bodies; row 7 Orra 1866 via '82 in 1948'. (Row 13 resolved wrongly to eleven.)
NT-14 $77.39 (Junia + Chronicle, broken by summing the lines); NT-18 great-niece (Chronicle + Falke main text, broken by Duncan and Falke's correction). Other pairs not identified as pairs.
A04 cannot be determined, works books burned 1931 (E#22). A06 not addressed. A10 abstained only in Section A, which doesn't count for E.
Junia's 'nothing before 1900' above the 1897 invoice; Duncan's 1868 vs 82 in 1948.
1897 pipettes, 16.72 vs 17.6, 5% low; 0.19 = 5% of 3.80; onset 1 May 1897 and cessation 12 June 1923 with nothing on farms changing. (3.85 for 1924 already deducted.)
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer and the ledger surplus.
Theft defeated by the 5 1/4% station gain (fat arrived heavy), 1911 interval, post-1923 rise.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214's <=0.05 in winter, nothing in summer, vs a flat 0.19.
A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware? No.'
A05 asserted: 'What the tester himself believed: that it was "something in the glass."'
Summary is 153 words, over the 150 cap.
Invoice, notebook, ledger, weigh book, test book, rival factory's figures, 1958 measurement.
No decoy adopted, no wrong headline figure.

Corruption: water circular sent to eleven families asserted as fact (Story 5, E#17)
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship resolved 'no relationship' (B4, E#14)
Gullibility A09: bookkeeper 'never' questioned the entries (D2)
Gullibility A03: manager 'never grasped' the understatement (D3 headline)
